title: Vermillion Clinic — triage LLM integration scratchpad
body:
Context:
- 30-min discovery with Vermillion Clinic clinical ops + IT (02/10). Small network of outpatient clinics (5 locations). EHR: Epic (hosted by a regional HCO partner).
- Goal: prototype a patient-facing triage assistant to collect symptom information, suggest next steps (tele-visit vs urgent), and surface care instructions. Not a diagnosis tool; must route to clinician when in doubt.

Key constraints (from call):
- PHI/HIPAA: logs with PHI are not allowed in hosted SaaS logs. Need either Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated with strict log redaction + customer-managed KMS.
- Data residency: patient data must stay in US region (East).
- Latency: aim for <= 350 ms 95p for short-turn prompts (single-turn symptom collection). For longer context/responses, they prefer streaming so patient gets progressive feedback.
- Throughput: expected peak 10 concurrent sessions per clinic = ~50 concurrent. POC can use 1-2 GPUs but need autoscale policy for Dedicated.
- EHR integration: Epic integration via FHIR (APIs) and HL7 v2 for legacy feeds. Read-only access to patient problem list and medications during POC. Writing back encounter notes needs clinical approval.
- Consent: must present explicit consent screen before collecting PHI. Need audit trail.

Initial product approach notes (rough):
- Deployment: Redwood Private in their VPC (preferred) to avoid PHI leakage risk. If not possible for POC, use Dedicated with customer-managed KMS + strict log redaction hooks.
- Model: start with an instruction-tuned open LLaMA-family variant we have verified (accuracy vs cost tradeoff). Offer a higher grade model for canary/critical routes.
- Prompting strategy: structured symptom intake flow with discrete slots (onset, severity, red flags). Use function-calling to normalize into FHIR Observation resources. Use schema + enum outputs where possible to reduce hallucination.
- Caching: prefix cache for standard triage flows (common symptom templates). KV caching across session to speed repeated prompts.
- Embeddings: patient history vector store (locally hosted or customer-managed vector DB). Use short-term session embedding to surface relevant past events. Ensure encryption at rest.
- Guardrails: deterministic verification steps for red flags (if model returns ambiguous safety-critical text, escalate to clinician). Add model output classifier (binary urgent/non-urgent) as ensemble with rule overrides.

Gotchas / open questions captured during call:
- Logging: they will not allow full transcript retention. Need token-level redaction or server-side filter that replaces PHI with placeholders before any analytics export. Who owns the filter? Ops or customer?
- FHIR mapping: several symptom fields are free-text on the Epic side — transformation rules will be fuzzy. Need product decision on how to map free-text to coded observations.
- Multilingual: initial pilot English-only, but Spanish support is priority in Q2 — impacts model selection and evaluation.
- Clinician workflow: where does the triage summary land? Inbox in Epic vs secure messaging. This will determine write-level permissions and audit logging requirements.
- Liability: legal wants explicit language in UI; clinical ops wants a quick escalation path. Need to align wording.
- Token cost: symtom intake + context embedding per session estimated ~150–500 tokens depending on verbosity. At scale this affects Dedicated sizing/pricing conversation.

Quick POC plan (3 sprints):
- Sprint 0 (1 week): security & compliance scoping + network access (SOW addendum). Deliverable: security checklist signed by HCO security. Owner: Tomás (due 2025-02-18).
- Sprint 1 (2 weeks): narrow scope triage flow + minimal FHIR read integration. Deliverable: working flow in staging with demo UI (no writeback). Owner: Mei (due 2025-03-04).
- Sprint 2 (2 weeks): add model guardrails, logging redaction hooks, streaming and latency tuning on Dedicated. Deliverable: pilot-ready deployment and runbook. Owner: Jordan (due 2025-03-18).
- Stakeholder review + clinical sign-off 1 week. Owner: Dr. Lila (due 2025-03-25).

Technical checklist / configuration notes (engineering-facing):
- Use Redwood Private control plane + customer VPC peering (preferred): ensure Egress rules block logs to external analytics unless redacted.
- Dedicated GPU pool options: start with 2x A10G nodes (quantized runtime) with autoscale threshold at 60% util. Consider 4x for higher concurrency.
- Model quantization: int8 path recommended for cost; measure latency/regression on representative prompts.
- Enable streaming API for patient UX; fall back to non-streaming for final summary to ensure consistency of guardrail checks.
- Function calling mapping: define 8 core functions for triage normalization (symptom_slot, redflag_check, severity_score, suggested_action, epicsave_stub, consent_record, language_detect, escalate_flag).
- Audit trails: persist action logs (who/when/which-version) to a customer-owned S3 (or equivalent). Avoid storing PHI in platform-level analytics buckets.

Risk register (high-level):
- Clinical safety risk (high): any hallucination that suggests harmful actions. Mitigation: rule-based red flag escalation + clinician-in-loop for high-risk outputs.
- Compliance risk (medium): accidental PHI leakage in logs. Mitigation: Private deployment, redaction, KMS.
- UX risk (low-medium): long response times if too much prior history is attached. Mitigation: windowed context + embeddings for retrieval.

Immediate action items (today/this week):
- Share this scratchpad with the team and schedule security sync. Owner: Aisha (today).
- Capture exact Epic FHIR endpoints and example payloads from Vermillion IT. Owner: Tomás (by 2025-02-16).
- Draft consent screen text (clinical + legal input). Owner: Dr. Lila + Mei (by 2025-02-20).
- Create Jira epic VC-9876 + link to this doc. Owner: Jordan (today).

Notes to self / heuristics learned in past pilots:
- Always include an explicit confirmation step before any write-to-EHR action; keep writes disabled for POC.
- Use deterministic templates for common symptom phrasing to reduce hallucination surface area.
- Keep patient-facing language conservative: "suggests" not "diagnoses".

Open questions to ask next meeting:
1) Can Vermillion provide a dev sandbox Epic FHIR endpoint? If yes, get creds and example patients.
2) Do they require data residency single-tenant nodes for pilot or is region-limited Dedicated acceptable?
3) Who signs off on clinical escalation thresholds (names/roles)?
4) Spanish support: any dialect specifics (medical Spanish preferred)?

Reference snippets to paste into proposals / email replies:
- Quick summary (for execs): "POC: patient triage assistant deployed in customer VPC. Structured intake → FHIR observation mapping → model-driven suggestion + clinician escalation. Focus on PHI-safe deployment and deterministic guardrails. Target pilot-ready in 6 weeks."
- Security blurb (for security review): "We propose Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS, network peering to the clinic VPC, audit logs written only to customer-owned storage, and token-level redaction hooks before any platform telemetry export."

End of scratchpad.
(Will keep iterating after Sec/IT sync on 02/14.)
